function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or run manually) to finish the task.  
I’ve also included the exact file contents you’ll need to create/overwrite.

> **⚠️ Important** – I can’t actually clone or push to your repo from here, but the commands below will do it for you on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> If you don’t have SSH keys set up, use HTTPS instead:
> `git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create the required files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create or overwrite `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – lightweight Node runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set maintainer (optional)
LABEL maintainer="Unknown"

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small and fast.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a clean install from `package-lock.json`.  
> * Exposes port **3000** – the common default for Node apps (adjust if your app uses another port).  
> * `CMD ["node", "app.js"]` runs the entry point; change `app.js` if your main file has a different name.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a directory for Kubernetes manifests (optional but tidy):

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
```

#### Deployment (`k8s/deployment.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

#### Service (`k8s/service.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # Service port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **Tip** – If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` and adjust the `port` accordingly.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create the workflow file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI / Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest \
            .

      # Push the image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What this does**  
> * Builds the image on every push to `main`.  
> * Tags it with the commit SHA and `latest`.  
> * Pushes to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`).  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication – no extra secrets needed.

> **If you prefer Docker Hub** replace the login and tags accordingly, e.g.:
> ```yaml
> with:
>   username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
>   password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
> ```
> and set the image name to `yourhub/nodejs-welcome`.

---

## 3️⃣ Stage the new/updated files

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml k8s/service.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

> If you created the `k8s` directory, add it too:
> `git add k8s/`

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run and build/push the Docker image.

---

### Quick sanity check

```bash
# Verify Dockerfile builds locally (optional)
docker build -t nodejs-welcome-test .

# Verify Kubernetes manifests (optional)
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/service.yaml
```

---

## Recap of what you now have

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas of the app |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app inside the cluster |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes Docker image on `main` |

You’re all set! 🎉 If you run into any issues (e.g., wrong port, missing environment variables), just tweak the files accordingly. Happy coding!
